messages:
acme_support: Hey team — customer reports SSE stream closing mid-response whenever the phone switches from carrier 5G to their phone hotspot. We see a partial JSON chunk then connection closes. Happened ~3x today. trace_id=trc_abc123 last_event_id=4829. Repro steps below, can someone triage? :frowning:

alisa_support: Thanks — can you paste the client SDK + platform and a small excerpt of the raw bytes you received (first 1KB after the cut)? Also confirm whether they use the browser EventSource or a mobile SDK.

acme_support: Using our Android client (embedded okhttp EventSource polyfill), SDK v2.4.1. Quick repro curl we ran locally:

```
curl -v \\n  -H "Authorization: Bearer xxxxx" \\n  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \\n  "https://api.redwood.com/v1/streams?model=gpt-test" \\n  --header "Last-Event-ID: 4829"
```

Partial payload they captured (truncated):

```
event: message
data: {"chunk":"The quick brown fox jumped over the lazy do",\n```

Then socket just closes on the client side with no final event.

ryan_oncall: Can you confirm exact client-side timestamp and the request start time (epoch) so we can correlate with edge logs? Also what IP/subnet the hotspot assigned? My first guess: NAT rebind from carrier -> hotspot is causing a TCP teardown at the NAT/CGNAT level. Please also check if the client sees a TCP RST.

acme_support: Sure — timestamps: start=3167778868 end=3167778886. Client IPs: 10.0.43.1 (phone hotspot) NAT to public 54.211.33.9 on FastCell network. We'll try to get a pcap.

devin_neteng: Likely NAT rebinding / different 5-tuple after switch. Two suggestions: (1) add an application-level SSE heartbeat (SSE comment) every 10-15s so middleboxes keep the flow alive, e.g. send `: ping\n\n` periodically, (2) make client reconnect logic tolerant and use `Last-Event-ID` to resume. Also tune kernel keepalive on any client-side box if applicable:

```
sysctl -w net.ipv4.tcp_keepalive_time=60
sysctl -w net.ipv4.tcp_keepalive_intvl=10
sysctl -w net.ipv4.tcp_keepalive_probes=6
```

Another common culprit is intermediate proxy/CDN idle timeout (Cloud CDN/nginx) closing the connection when the path swaps.

alisa_support: Good call. acme_support, do we see any 499/connection closed by client or 502/504 from upstream in the logs? If so post the edge request id. Also check whether your phone's hotspot enforces an idle timeout when bridging 5G->WiFi.

deploy-bot: [link] Edge trace trc_abc123: observed client close (499) at 3167778887, no upstream error returned. Log snippet:

```
edge: request_id=trc_abc123 client_ip=54.211.33.9 status=499 bytes_sent=2340 tls=true path=/v1/streams
```

acme_support: We saw that 499 in the edge logs as well. Curious about billing — will the partial chunk be billed? Customer is worried about being charged for incomplete responses.

ryan_oncall: Short answer: yes, tokens/compute until the point the model streamed are generally billable. If you think there's an SDK bug causing premature close, open a billing dispute and we'll review. For the technical fix: implement robust reconnect + server-side small checkpoints (Last-Event-ID) so the client can resume.

alisa_support: For immediate mitigation, try two things: (A) have the client send a small SSE comment every 10s `: keepalive\n\n`, (B) treat any abrupt close as retryable and reconnect with exponential backoff passing `Last-Event-ID`. That should avoid lost user-perceived completions.

devin_neteng: If you can provide a pcap of the switch event we can confirm if there's an RST or if the NAT simply stops mapping. If it's RST from the phone hotspot NAT, nothing much we can do server-side except recommend the keepalive heartbeat and reconnect.

acme_support: Will collect pcap and try heartbeat + reconnect. One more question: any server-side knobs we can enable (on the Redwood side) to reduce chance of partial JSON? Maybe buffer until full event before sending?

ryan_oncall: We intentionally stream as produced to keep latency low. Buffering server-side would increase latency and cost. Better to make the client resilient. If a large number of customers are impacted we can consider increasing minimum chunk flush granularity, but let's wait for pcap & frequency metrics.

acme_support: Got it. Trying quick client patch now (adds SSE comment ping + Last-Event-ID resume). I'll report back in ~30m with outcome or pcap. Thanks all :thumbsup:

ryan_oncall: thanks — if it persists and you have a reproducible case, set up a Zoom with network capture and we can do a joint debug. :eyes:
